title: AI-agnostic decision review pipeline
summary: Planning reviews currently force people to reconstruct the proposed direction from task-heavy output. We chose to keep JSON as the source of truth while giving plans and brainstorms separate, self-contained review experiences. This plan puts a plain-language overview first, connects requirements to observable behavior and proof, and keeps implementation dossiers collapsed until someone is ready to execute. The result is a reviewer who can understand the problem, the chosen direction, what will change, and the expected outcome before opening a single task.
problem: Planning output is technically valid but too sparse and task-centric for a reviewer to understand the recommendation, evidence, tradeoffs, and approval gates without reconstructing the reasoning from execution waves.

decision.question: Approve direct AI-authored HTML as the default review experience?
decision.recommendation: Keep JSON as the source of truth, let the active AI design each review page, and promote it only after static safety and decision-fidelity validation.
rationale: A recommendation is reviewable only when its evidence, rejected alternatives, and accepted tradeoffs are visible together.
The active AI can adapt information design to the specific decision instead of flattening every plan into one layout.
A provider-neutral static validator preserves offline safety without becoming another presentation framework.
decision.acceptedTradeoff: Review HTML is intentionally nondeterministic and disposable; canonical JSON and validation carry the durable contract.

outcome.goal: A reviewer can understand and approve the proposed direction in under five minutes before opening the execution appendix.
doneWhen: The plain-language problem, chosen direction, expected changes, outcome, and human gate are visible before implementation detail.
Evidence, architecture, alternatives, risks, and validation have distinct semantic treatments.
The accepted artifact opens without network access in supported AI hosts.
Quick plans remain concise while standard and deep plans carry decision-grade detail.

in: Portable AI-authored plan and brainstorm review flow
constraints: Self-contained HTML with no external assets
Backward compatibility with valid v3 quick artifacts

solution_shape.summary: Transform one validated decision artifact into semantic review sections while preserving JSON as the authoritative, portable record.
dataFlow: Agent writes a contract-v3 JSON artifact
The active AI selects the plan or brainstorm composition
The AI encodes evidence, tradeoffs, and gates in task-appropriate HTML
The validator rejects unsafe or decision-incomplete candidates
Reviewer opens a self-contained HTML dossier and makes the decision

added: Plain-language plan summary before implementation detail
Distinct plan and brainstorm information architectures
Visible brainstorming divergence, clustering, and convergence
modified: AI-authored review guidance and static safety validation
Execution appendix defaults collapsed and appears last
removed: Shared generic-card hierarchy for both artifact types
Expanded task dossiers competing with the decision narrative
unchanged: JSON remains the source of truth

scenarios.given: A standard or deep plan has been generated
scenarios.then: change deltas, scenarios, coverage, readiness, and task interfaces are required

scenarios.given: A reviewer opens the generated plan HTML
scenarios.when: they scan from the decision through execution
scenarios.then: they can trace each requirement to scenarios, tasks, and concrete verification

scenarios.given: A valid quick plan omits architecture-grade ceremony
scenarios.then: it stays concise and remains decision-useful

research.finding: The previous sample was generated from a minimal quick-plan lifecycle fixture.
research.consequence: It demonstrated compatibility but could not demonstrate the intended standard/deep review experience.

evidence.claim: The deleted fixed renderer flattened most nested values into generic definition lists and cards.
evidence.source: git history for the removed portable renderer
evidence.implication: The active AI should choose a review hierarchy suited to each artifact.

evidence.claim: The end-to-end lifecycle sample used depth quick with empty alternatives, risks, assumptions, and open questions.
evidence.implication: Compatibility fixtures and showcase fixtures must be separate.

evidence.claim: Decision-first review works best when the recommendation, evidence, options, and human gate are visually connected.
evidence.implication: The top of the page should act as a compact executive decision brief.

evidence.claim: Bundled guidance plus a stdlib validator is portable without a template or provider dependency.
evidence.implication: Keep presentation generation agent-owned and validate only safety and decision fidelity.

evidence.claim: Every future host will support the same local-file preview behavior.
evidence.implication: HTML is an enhancement; JSON and Markdown guidance remain the durable fallback.

alternatives.name: Keep a fixed review template
alternatives.summary: Improve spacing and color while continuing to project every artifact through one maintained layout.
tradeoffs: Important evidence and tradeoffs remain visually indistinguishable
Reviewers still reconstruct the decision narrative themselves
alternatives.reasonNotSelected: It treats an information-architecture failure as a styling problem.
alternatives.conditionsWouldChange: Reconsider only if AI-authored reviews prove too inconsistent after measured use.

alternatives.name: Adopt a client-side template framework
alternatives.summary: Bundle a component runtime and hydrate the artifact into an interactive application.
alternatives.reasonNotSelected: The current requirement is a review document, not an editing application.
alternatives.conditionsWouldChange: Reconsider when reviewers need annotations, state changes, or collaborative editing.

alternatives.name: Use Markdown only
alternatives.summary: Emit a long-form Markdown decision record and rely on each host preview.
alternatives.reasonNotSelected: It cannot reliably provide the full-width, structured approval experience requested.
alternatives.conditionsWouldChange: Retain Markdown as an accessibility and host-capability fallback.

assumptions.assumption: Reviewers open generated HTML in a modern browser.
assumptions.validation: Keep the JSON artifact readable and document the fallback.

assumptions.assumption: Three to five evidence items are enough for a standard decision review.
assumptions.impactIfWrong: The dossier may be either shallow or noisy.
assumptions.validation: Evaluate representative real plans and tune guidance rather than hard-coding a maximum.

open_questions.question: Should a future version support reviewer annotations?
open_questions.resolution: Defer until static review behavior is validated.

decisions_for_approval.decision: Use the semantic decision dossier as the default plan and brainstorm HTML review.

risks.risk: Dense documents become visually exhausting on smaller screens.
risks.trigger: The page produces horizontal body overflow or cards collapse below readable widths.
risks.mitigation: Use responsive grids, readable line lengths, and isolate wide tables in labeled scroll regions.
risks.recovery: Fall back to a single-column document flow while preserving section order.

risks.risk: AI-authored review HTML omits decision-critical fields.
risks.trigger: A valid candidate lacks the canonical approval question, recommendation, or outcome.
risks.mitigation: Require canonical decision strings in the visible lead before promotion.
risks.recovery: Regenerate once from JSON, then fall back to the same decision hierarchy in chat.

risks.risk: The richer design introduces an external runtime dependency.
risks.trigger: Generated HTML references a script, font, stylesheet, or network URL.
risks.mitigation: Keep CSS inline, JavaScript absent, and enforce no-external-asset tests.
risks.recovery: Remove the dependency and regenerate the self-contained artifact.

validation.strategy: Validate canonical JSON, reject unsafe or decision-incomplete HTML, exercise portable installs, and inspect representative AI-authored pages.
definitionOfDone: Rich plan and brainstorm fixtures pass canonical and portable validators.
Every decision-critical field appears in the generated review.
The page has no body overflow at 320, 768, 1440, and 1920 pixels.
Generated HTML contains no script or external asset reference.

coverage.requirement: Generate a distinct implementation dossier for plans
checks: Plan HTML contains the change ledger, behavior scenarios, and coverage spine before execution

coverage.requirement: Generate a distinct exploration workbench for brainstorming
checks: Brainstorm HTML exposes framing, divergence, clustering, convergence, dissent, and direction gate
Generated documents have no external assets and no body overflow at tested widths
Focused, lifecycle, portability, and full test suites pass

reasons: The canonical contract is explicit, traceable, and covered by representative fixtures.
The AI-authored page remains an offline, disposable projection of canonical JSON.
unresolved: Live reviewer annotation remains deliberately out of scope.

tasks.description: Define the plan review authoring contract
tasks.action: Tell the active AI to lead with the decision brief and choose suitable HTML for outcome, scope, architecture, evidence, alternatives, risks, validation, and the execution appendix.
acceptance_criteria: Decision and human gate lead the document
The AI chooses task-appropriate semantic HTML without a template kit
tasks.risk: Generation guidance may be too vague for consistent decision-first output.
tasks.recovery: Refine the content contract without introducing a renderer or component kit.

tasks.description: Define the brainstorm review authoring contract
tasks.action: Tell the active AI to present a recommendation spine, decision frame, evidence, experiment, comparison, and approach dossiers.
acceptance_criteria: Each approach exposes benefits, tradeoffs, failure mode, and selection conditions
tasks.risk: Options may appear repetitive without strong generation guidance.
tasks.recovery: Reject duplicate candidate spines during artifact review.

tasks.description: Add static review safety and fidelity validation
tasks.action: Validate bounded self-contained HTML, exact CSP, safe static markup, visible canonical decision text, and atomic promotion.
acceptance_criteria: Unsafe or network-capable HTML is rejected
Decision-critical text must appear before collapsible details
A failed candidate never replaces the accepted page
tasks.risk: Static checks accept an obfuscated network or hidden-content construct.
tasks.recovery: Add the bypass as a regression and tighten the conservative validation boundary.

tasks.description: Prove rich, quick, copied, and symlinked review paths
tasks.action: Keep representative deep JSON fixtures, quick lifecycle coverage, and copied or symlinked validator execution tests.
acceptance_criteria: Rich fixtures exercise every evidence state and major review section
Canonical and portable validation preserve the same decision contract
tasks.risk: Tests can accidentally prescribe the AI's layout.
tasks.recovery: Assert only safety, visible decision fidelity, portability, and canonical JSON behavior.
